title: acre-gui draws its window with una
body:
`acre-gui` draws its window with eframe 0.37 and egui. falx-gui moved from eframe to the una UI kit in falx commit d093a3f, and acre-gui follows. The port issue on una's side is una-aa4ff6, which lists the una widgets acre-gui would want: a tree, a number field, a colour picker, a box that draws pixels and multi-line text entry. None of them exists yet. Jack chose to port now and do without them, with a una issue for each gap.

The egui-free modules stay as they are: `anchor`, `arrange`, `document`, `handle`, `neovim`, `nudge`, `playback`, `recent`, `reorder`, `selection`, `snap`, `tabs` and `tool`.

## Proposal

- una is a path dependency on `../../../una`, as in falx-gui. eframe and rfd leave `Cargo.toml`.
- `link.rs` takes a wake function in place of `egui::Context`. `drag.rs` and `view.rs` take acre-gui's own point and vector types in place of `Pos2` and `Vec2`.
- The canvas is one una `Surface`. acre renders the view at the pane's pixel size with `acre::render::draw_view`. acre-gui then draws the grid, selection, handles, guides, anchors and previews onto the same pixmap with tiny-skia and presents it. While a pan or zoom settles, `Surface::view` stretches the last buffer. 100% zoom is one screen pixel per canvas pixel, since una does not expose the window's scale (una-f17e35).
- The toolbar, tabs, status line and transport are rows of una widgets. The File menu is a una `menu_button`. Open uses una's `pick_file` with the pattern `*.acre`.
- The time bar is a second `Surface` drawn with tiny-skia. Section titles move from the bar into a tooltip.
- The sections and properties panels become fixed columns beside the canvas, in place of overlays.
- Properties: numbers and colours are one-line una fields, a colour written as hex, with the "none" toggle kept. The font is a una dropdown.
- The node text field is a one-line una field on a popup layer at the node.
- Space, the arrows, Delete, Backspace, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V keep their meanings and gain no new chords.
- The close button and the compositor's close request both open a una dialog.

## Out of scope

- Shift+Enter in the node text field, until una has multi-line entry (una-d1d8cd).
- The pointer shape over handles, until a una `Surface` can set one.
- Pinch zoom, which acre-gui never had.

## Cost

acre-gui's version moves at release, not in this work. The changelog gets the changes under `[Unreleased]`.
close_reason: Landed in e8db7f9 on dev, with the decisions in the notes here. Follow-ups: acre-0ad3c5 (decade's close request waits on the dialog), acre-e0fda6 (SIGTERM ignored) and acre-5c6621 (multi-line node text). The una gaps are filed under una-aa4ff6.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: The node text field is a one-line una `field`, so a line break shows in it as the two characters `\n` and a `\n` typed there writes a line break. Enter, Tab or a click elsewhere writes the text, and Escape closes the field without writing, since una reports Escape as `cancelled`. Shift+Enter writes as Enter does until una has multi-line entry (una-d1d8cd).

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: Space, the arrow keys, Delete and Backspace are una commands with those chords, because a bound command wins over a focused button and una keeps plain-key chords from a text field. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V are read from `Ui::events`, since a ctrl chord bound as a command would take them from a text field; acre-gui skips them while one of its own fields has the keys. `App::keys` declares no command while the close dialog, the file picker or the recent files list shows, so their arrow keys and Escape reach them. A una menu or dropdown that is open still loses the arrow keys to the commands.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: una's `menu_button` has no submenus and no hover signal for an entry, so File > Open Recent… opens a list built in `App::recent_list` on the popup layer, a button per file, with the preview of the file under the pointer beside it as a una image. una's `tabs` gives no signal per tab, so a tab's full path moved from a hover tooltip to the status line alone.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: Handles, outlines, the snap and anchor reaches and the polygon's close circle are sized in points of `unit` pixels, where `unit` is the chrome font's cell height over the small style's mockup height of 18. With no window scale from una (una-f17e35) this keeps handles grabbable on a scaled screen, while the zoom stays one screen pixel per canvas pixel at 100%.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: With `--stdio`, the stdin thread in `Link::stdio` ends the process when stdin closes, as falx-gui's does, since una runs no frame while the compositor hides the window (una-a928af). Replies to the editor still go out from `App::talk` in a frame, so a hidden window answers once it is shown again.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6787394a
notes.text: File > Edit in neovim is always clickable, and when it cannot open neovim it names the reason on the status line, as falx-gui's command does, since a una menu entry shows no tooltip for being unavailable.
